answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with escrowed identity bonds: to draw paid work from the shared task lagoon, each agent locks a stake co-signed by two established peers. Fake identities forfeit the stake, and co-signers lose a share too, so vouching for fakes is costly. Farming identities then resembles drilling a barren shale field — each new identity costs another bond and two more bribes while the lagoon's rewards split ever thinner. Each proven fraud leaves a public slash record, a plume of evidence staining the vouching chain, until the Nth Sybil costs more than it can earn.
